data.segment_title: Campaign 2008 / Obama vs. McCain / Early Voting
data.segment_description:
(Studio: Charles Gibson)  How early voting is sweeping the nation reported; map shown of states with the heaviest balloting.  

(New York: John Berman)  The phenomenon  of early voting featured; scenes shown of lines in Florida, Georgia, Nevada.  [Florida VOTER, Georgia voter Richard FRANCIS, Nevada VOTER, Gwinnett County, Georgia, elections director Lynn LEDFORD†, Reed College early voting center professor Paul GRONKE†, University of Virginia professor Larry SABATO†, Senator Barack OBAMA&nbsp- comment on early voting.]  The vote for Obama over Senator John McCain in early voting according to the ABC News/"Washington Post" poll cited.  

(Studio: Charles Gibson)  The quarterly GDP figures and record profits for ExxonMobil cited.  

(Virginia Beach, Virginia: Jake Tapper)  The campaign patterns for both presidential candidates with five days left featured; Obama TV ad shown.  [BIDEN&nbsp- blames eight years of failed economic policies for the GDP numbers; states it is time to change drivers.]  [Yesterday on ABC, OBAMA&nbsp- says he would return to the Senate if he lost.]  [McCAIN&nbsp- jokes about Obama; comments on ExxonMobil's profits.]  [Senator Joe BIDEN&nbsp- says the ExxonMobils do not need a tax break.]  [In Erie, Governor Sarah PALIN&nbsp- speaks about the terrorist threat.]  The nature of the campaign attacks carried out by Obama and McCain compared.  

(Studio: Charles Gibson)  The standings of McCain and Obama in the ABC News/"Washington Post" four-day tracking poll cited.  

(Studio: Charles Gibson; Washington: George Stephanopoulos)  The extraordinary early voting and the arguments against it with examples for earlier elections and the centrality of the economy to the election discussed.  

(Studio: Charles Gibson)  The audience for last night's broadcast of an infomercial by Obama cited.  [Yesterday, OBAMA&nbsp- says the amount of money we raised has been extraordinary and we expanded the pool of small donors under the FEC guidelines.]

(Studio: Charles Gibson)  Report introduced.   (London: Nick Watt)  The refugee crisis in Congo due to the rapidly escalating conflict and the ineffectiveness of a U.N. presence featured; scenes shown of rebel soldiers, panic in Goma, rockets being fired, debris and bodies in the streets.  [Voice of International Rescue Committee-Congo Bob KITCHEN†- says the people here have nothing.]
